business_model.claim: Alpha Metallurgical Resources is a Tennessee-based mining company operating coal mines and preparation and load-out facilities in Virginia and West Virginia across the CAPP coal basin, employing approximately 3,860 people and holding a 65.0% interest in the DTA coal export terminal.
quotes: We are a Tennessee-based mining company with operations in Virginia and West Virginia.
We own a 65.0% interest in Dominion Terminal Associates (“DTA”), a coal export terminal in Newport News, Virginia.
We operate high-quality, cost-competitive met coal mines across the CAPP coal basin.
As of September 30, 2026, our operations consisted of twenty active mines and eight active coal preparation and load-out facilities, with approximately 3,860 employees.

business_model.claim: The company generates coal sales from coal produced and processed at its own operations as well as coal purchased from third-party producers for blending or resale.
quotes: We market coal produced at our operations and purchase and resell coal mined by others.

Our coal volumes include coal produced and processed by us, our “captive coal,” as well as coal purchased from third-party producers to blend with our produced coal in order to meet customer specifications.
We also sell coal produced by others, some of which is processed and/or blended with coal produced from our mines prior to resale, with the remainder purchased for resale.

business_model.claim: Metallurgical coal is the company's primary product, accounting for 96% of coal revenues in 2025 and 97% in 2024, while thermal coal is produced and sold as a byproduct.
quotes: Met coal accounted for approximately 96% and 97%, respectively, of our coal revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.
We produce, process, and sell met coal and thermal coal as a byproduct.

business_model.claim: By 2025 shipment tonnage, the company's metallurgical coal sales mix consisted of 34% High Vol-A, 31% High Vol-B, 21% Mid Vol, and 14% Low Vol coal.
quotes: 34% High Vol-A 31% High Vol-B 21% Mid Vol 14% Low Vol
1 For full-year 2025 shipments, by tonnage.

business_model.claim: Beyond coal sales, the company generates other revenues (4,471 in the 9 months ended Sep. 30, 2026; table in USD thousands) from equipment sales, rentals, terminal and processing fees, analysis fees, royalties, and natural gas, and records freight and handling fulfillment revenue within coal revenues.
quotes: In addition, we generate other revenues from equipment sales, rentals, terminal and processing fees, coal and environmental analysis fees, royalties and the sale of natural gas.

We also record freight and handling fulfillment revenue within coal revenues for freight and handling services provided in delivering coal to certain customers, which are a component of the contractual selling price.

business_model.claim: The company sells metallurgical coal to domestic and international steel and coke producers for steel production, and sells thermal coal primarily to large utilities and industrial customers for power generation and industrial uses.
quotes: We predominantly produce metallurgical (“met”) coal, which is shipped to domestic and international steel and coke producers.
Purchases of our met coal were made primarily in several countries in Asia, Europe, South America, and the northeastern and midwestern regions of the United States for purposes of steel production.
Purchases of our thermal coal were made primarily for purposes of power generation and industrial uses both in the United States and across the world.

business_model.claim: Most coal revenue comes from exports—73% in 2025 and 78% in 2024, with Asia accounting for 45% of export coal revenues in 2025—and all sales are conducted in U.S. dollars.
quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 approximately 73% and 78%, respectively, of our coal revenues were derived from coal sales made to customers outside the United States.

Asia was our largest export market for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, with coal sales to Asia accounting for approximately 45% and 43%, respectively, of export coal revenues and 33% and 34%, respectively, of coal revenues in each year.
All of our sales are conducted in U.S. dollars.

business_model.claim: Customer concentration is high: in 2025, coal sales to the largest customer represented approximately 14% of total revenues and sales to the 10 largest customers represented approximately 77%.
quotes: Coal sales to our largest customer during the year ended December 31, 2025 accounted for approximately 14% of our total revenues, and coal sales to our 10 largest customers accounted for approximately 77% of our total revenues.

business_model.claim: The company manages commodity price risk through coal supply agreements, using annual fixed-price contracts for domestic met customers and index-linked or other pricing mechanisms for exports; for 2026, 87% of metallurgical coal was committed and priced, and 3.5 million tons were committed to domestic customers for 2027.
quotes: We manage our commodity price risk for coal sales through the use of coal supply agreements.
Domestic met customers typically enter into one-year agreements with a fixed price for the entire contract year.
As of October 29, 2026, Alpha has committed and priced approximately 87% of its metallurgical coal for 2026 at an average price of $126.69 per ton.
Alpha has committed approximately 3.5 million tons of metallurgical coal to domestic customers for shipment in the 2027 calendar year at an average price of $135.48 per ton.

business_model.claim: The company operates and reports under a single reportable operating segment, Met, which encompasses both metallurgical and incidental thermal coal shipments.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we have one reportable operating segment: Met.
As of September 30, 2026, we have one reportable segment: Met.

business_model.claim: Revenues are primarily driven by metallurgical coal prices and sales volumes, which depend on global steel demand, manufacturing activity, tariffs and trade policies, geopolitical conditions, and supply disruptions.
quotes: Our results of operations depend substantially upon the prices we receive for our coal.

As discussed in the “Market Overview” presented above, metallurgical coal prices remain at lower levels than in recent years due to weak global steel demand which has been influenced by a slowdown in manufacturing activity.
Economic pressures, geopolitical uncertainty, and shifting trade policies have contributed to metallurgical market challenges.

While global steel demand remains weak, supply-related factors, such as mine closure announcements, temporarily influenced metallurgical coal indices to rise toward the end of the third quarter, with further volatility continuing after the quarter close.

business_model.claim: Realized coal revenue per ton is also driven by coal quality (volatility and heat content), regional supply and demand, FOB mine versus FOB shipping port contract conventions, and export terminal availability such as at DTA.
quotes: Our realized price per ton of coal is influenced by many factors that vary by region, including (i) coal quality, which includes energy (heat content), sulfur, ash, volatile matter and moisture content; (ii) differences in market conventions concerning transportation costs and volume measurement; and (iii) regional supply and demand.
Coal volatility is a significant factor influencing met coal pricing as coal with a lower volatility has historically been more highly valued and typically commands a higher price in the market.

In addition, coal sales volumes increased 1.6% compared to the prior year period driven largely by changes in the timing of shipments as DTA’s planned equipment outage in June delayed certain shipments into the current quarter.

business_model.claim: Increased adoption of non-coke steelmaking processes in North America, coal industry overcapacity, and U.S. dollar appreciation against foreign currencies can structurally reduce demand and realized prices for the company's coal.
quotes: The North American steel industry increasingly relies on processes to make steel that do not use coke, such as electric arc furnaces or pulverized coal processes.
Subsequent overcapacity in the industry contributed, and may in the future contribute, to lower coal prices.

Coal is priced internationally in U.S. dollars, and, as a result, general economic conditions in foreign markets and changes in foreign currency exchange rates may provide our foreign competitors with a competitive advantage.

business_model.claim: The company's largest operating expense is cost of coal sales, totaling $1,924,691 in 2025 and 1,427,708 in the 9 months ended Sep. 30, 2026 (tables in USD thousands), driven by operating supplies, repairs and maintenance, purchased coal, royalties, wages and benefits, freight and handling, and selling taxes.
quotes: Cost of coal sales (exclusive of items shown separately below) | $1,924,691 | $2,451,601 | $(526,910) | (21.5)%
Cost of coal sales (exclusive of items shown separately below) | 509,656 | 461,635 | 1,427,708 | 1,446,172

Our primary expenses are for operating supply costs, repair and maintenance expenditures, costs of purchased coal, royalties, wages and benefits, freight and handling costs and taxes incurred in selling our coal.

business_model.claim: Unit costs fluctuate with sales volume, export freight mix, coal-price-linked royalties and taxes, purchased coal levels, input price volatility (such as fuel, explosives, steel, tires, contract services, and healthcare), and decisions to idle or reduce higher-cost mines.
quotes: We experience volatility in operating costs related to fuel, explosives, steel, tires, contract services and healthcare, among others, and take measures to mitigate the increases in these costs at all operations.

Average cost of coal sales per ton decreased 12.0% compared to the prior year period, due in part to a reduction in freight and handling costs as a relatively lower percentage of export sales resulted in lower rail and ocean vessel freight costs.
The lower coal pricing environment reduced royalties and taxes.

In addition, lower levels of purchased coal and the ongoing impact of cost reduction efforts, including wage reductions during the second quarter of 2025, as well as the impact of previous decisions to reduce relatively higher-cost production sources served to reduce costs on a per ton basis.

business_model.claim: Beyond direct mining costs, results are affected by geologic conditions, permitting and regulatory compliance, depreciation, depletion and amortization, SG&A, equity losses in affiliates, and long-term obligations for workers' compensation and black lung (183,438), pensions (67,108), and asset retirement (200,994) as of Sep. 30, 2026 (table in USD thousands).
quotes: We may also experience difficult geologic conditions, delays in obtaining permits, labor shortages, unforeseen equipment problems, and unexpected shortages of critical materials such as tires, fuel and explosives that may result in adverse cost increases and limit our ability to produce at forecasted levels.

These factors have had and will continue to have a significant effect on our costs of production and competitive position and, as a result, on our results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
